primary_task: Start a remote iOS simulator session on EAS cloud with `npx --yes eas-cli@latest simulator:start`, install the user's app build, drive it with agent-device (open, snapshot, press, screenshot), then stop the session.

requirements.name: eas-cli (via npx)
requirements.basis: install packages from the open registries (pip from PyPI, npm, apt from Ubuntu, go modules, nuget, GitHub release downloads), build, test, run CLIs and scripts

requirements.name: agent-device (via npx)
requirements.evidence: This skill uses **agent-device** (open source, MIT), run on demand via `npx agent-device@latest`
requirements.basis: install packages from the open registries (pip from PyPI, npm, apt from Ubuntu, go modules, nuget, GitHub release downloads)

requirements.name: expo-account (EXPO_TOKEN or eas login)
requirements.evidence: **Authenticated.** Interactive machine → `npx --yes eas-cli@latest login`. **Cloud sandbox / CI / headless agent has no browser login — set `EXPO_TOKEN`** (expo.dev → Account → Access Tokens)
requirements.basis: accounts, logins, API keys or credentials for external services other than the listed connectors and GitHub (cloud providers such as AWS, Azure and GCP, SaaS products, model hubs, app stores, email delivery, payment)

requirements.name: EAS Simulator service (expo.dev / EAS infrastructure)
requirements.evidence: EAS Simulator runs a remote iOS simulator or Android emulator on EAS infrastructure that you drive from your machine
requirements.basis: other hosts are refused (for example huggingface, Microsoft Learn and Azure, Cloudflare, Expo, Neon and NVIDIA)

requirements.name: expo.dev
requirements.evidence: npx --yes eas-cli@latest simulator:availability --json ... npx --yes eas-cli@latest simulator:start --platform ios --type agent-device --non-interactive
requirements.basis: egress_deny: "expo.dev", "*.expo.dev"; network access to hosts outside the egress allow-list: only PyPI, npm, GitHub, Ubuntu apt archives, NuGet and the Go module proxy are open; other hosts are refused, for example huggingface.co, Microsoft Learn and Azure endpoints, Cloudflare, Expo, Neon and NVIDIA

requirements.name: app build (dev build or release .app; Mode C needs a dev build built locally on a Mac or on EAS Build)
requirements.evidence: The remote sim boots **blank — no Expo Go, no apps.** Install a build, then drive it ... Mac → dev client builds locally; no Mac → build it on EAS (`developmentClient: true`).
requirements.basis: Windows or macOS, and their GUI toolchains (Xcode, Visual Studio, PowerShell on Windows); EAS Build also needs the Expo account under "accounts, logins, API keys or credentials for external services other than the listed connectors and GitHub"

requirements.name: local simulator/emulator (fallback when EAS Simulator is not available)
requirements.evidence: Fall back to their normal local path for the actual goal — `expo run:ios` / Xcode / Android Studio for a local sim/emulator
requirements.basis: physical devices and hardware: phones, emulators, boards, cameras

notes: The whole task runs against Expo's hosted EAS service; the session has no Expo credential and Expo hosts are refused by the proxy. The document's fallback (local simulator via expo run:ios / Xcode / Android Studio) is also not possible here (no macOS, no emulators), so no reading makes the primary task achievable. Mode C tunnel (`expo start --tunnel`) would also need an external tunnel host not in the allow-list. Under a reading where the only deliverable is telling the user EAS Simulator is unavailable, the agent could do that, but that is not the primary task.
